newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Judgment unlikely to lower NGC '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Judgment unlikely to lower NGC '97 profit.

text.p: Natural Gas Corporation said on Friday the recent High Court judgment on the Kapuni gas supply dispute was unlikely to have an adverse impact on the company's results for the year to June 30, 1997.
Chief executive Richard Bentley said the damages awarded could make a positive contribution to the year's results.
Bentley said Natural Gas welcomed confirmation of its interpretation of the Kapuni gas contract, in particular that the contract continues in force for the life of the field.
However, it was disappointed that aspects of the contract were found to have an anti-competitive effect.
Bentley said the court's judgment that the contract remained in force ensured a continued supply of gas to Kapuni Gas Contracts Limited, for supply to the petrochemical plants and to Natural Gas.

However, that supply was reduced by the court's ruling over the competitive effect of the contract, which directed that half the gas left in the Kapuni Field was awarded to Shell and Todd without compensation to the buyer under the contract.
Bentley said this lack of compensation did not appear consistent with the upholding of the contract and the rights it conferred to the buyer.

"Our evaluation of this lengthy and complex judgement is continuing. We have reached no conclusions at this time as to whether the finding relating to the Commerce Act will be appealed," Bentley said.

He said the impact on Natural Gas of the reduced supply depended on several factors to be negotiated with Shell and Todd. They included the quantity of gas remaining in the field, the profiles for delivery of that gas and the price.

Bentley noted the court's finding that Natural Gas was entitled to damages from Shell and Todd over their unjustified use of Kapuni Gas, including gas used for certain field-related purposes and gas supplied to the Kiwi dairy factory near Hawera.
The amount payable to Natural Gas had yet to be quantified, and would be determined by the court if it could not be settled by agreement.

Bentley said the overall financial impact on Natural Gas would be substantially mitigated by an indemnity given by Fletcher Challenge to Natural Gas, which related to losses arising from matters affecting the enforceability of the Kapuni Gas Contract.
